es: Reconocer peticiones muy indirectas (I don't suppose you could, would it be at all possible, I was wondering if) y elegir el grado de indirección que pide cada situación.

teaching.en: I don't suppose you could lend me your ladder.
teaching.es: No creo que pudieras prestarme tu escalera, ¿verdad?
teaching.explanationEs: I don't suppose you could + verbo base es la petición más indirecta: espera un «no» y deja una salida fácil.
teaching.audioText: I don't suppose you could lend me your ladder.

teaching.en: Would it be at all possible to borrow the ladder until Sunday?
teaching.es: ¿Sería posible en absoluto tomar prestada la escalera hasta el domingo?
teaching.explanationEs: Would it be (at all) possible to + verbo: muy formal; at all suaviza todavía más.
segments: Would it be at all possible
to borrow the ladder until Sunday?
teaching.audioText: Would it be at all possible to borrow the ladder until Sunday?

teaching.en: I was wondering if you might do me a favour.
teaching.es: Me preguntaba si podrías hacerme un favor.
teaching.explanationEs: I was wondering if + might/could: el pasado crea distancia y suena cortés, no dudoso.
teaching.audioText: I was wondering if you might do me a favour.

teaching.en: Would you mind lending me the ladder for an hour?
teaching.es: ¿Te importaría prestarme la escalera una hora?
teaching.explanationEs: Would you mind + verbo en -ing: petición cortés y algo más indirecta que Could you…?
teaching.audioText: Would you mind lending me the ladder for an hour?

teaching.en: Could you lend me the ladder?
teaching.es: ¿Podrías prestarme la escalera?
teaching.explanationEs: Could you…? es la petición neutra: sirve con casi todos si el favor es pequeño.
teaching.audioText: Could you lend me the ladder?

teaching.en: Our neighbour is very polite, so she never gives orders.
teaching.es: Nuestra vecina es muy educada, así que nunca da órdenes.
teaching.explanationEs: Una orden como «Lend me the ladder» solo encaja entre amigos muy cercanos.
teaching.audioText: Our neighbour is very polite, so she never gives orders.

prompt.es: Elige la petición más indirecta para pedirle una bici a un vecino.

choices.text: Can you lend me your bike?
I don't suppose you could lend me your bike.
Lend me your bike.

feedback.es: I don't suppose you could es la fórmula más indirecta: usa could y espera un posible no. Can you y la orden son más directas.

hint.es: Busca la fórmula que empieza con I don't suppose y lleva could.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Sería posible en absoluto pedir prestado tu libro?»

feedback.es: La fórmula Would it be at all possible to… pide un favor con mucha formalidad; possible es el adjetivo clave.

origin.text: Would it be at all ___ to borrow your book?

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Podrías ayudarme con esta maleta, por favor?»

answer.text: Could you help me with this suitcase please
accepted: Could you help me with this suitcase please
Could you please help me with this suitcase

feedback.es: Could you + verbo base forma la petición neutra y please la suaviza al final.

hint.es: Empieza con Could you y termina con please.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada petición con su grado de indirección.

pairs: Could you lend me the keys?
I was wondering if you might lend me the keys.
I don't suppose you could lend me the keys.

feedback.es: Cada fórmula sube un grado: la orden es directa, Could you es neutra, wondering es indirecta y I don't suppose es la más indirecta.

pairs: Could you lend me the keys?
I was wondering if you might lend me the keys.
I don't suppose you could lend me the keys.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace la viajera en la estación.

choices.text: She orders a stranger to carry her bag.
She thanks a stranger for watching her bag.
She makes a very polite request to a stranger.

feedback.es: La viajera usa «I don't suppose you could» con una persona desconocida para un favor pequeño: es una petición muy cortés.

origin.audio: Excuse me. I don't suppose you could watch my bag for a minute while I buy a ticket?

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Te importaría cerrar la puerta?»

feedback.es: Would you mind + verbo en -ing es la petición cortés; mind es el verbo clave.

origin.text: Would you ___ closing the door?

prompt.es: Elige la petición adecuada para pedir un favor grande a tu jefa.

choices.text: I was wondering if I might leave early on Friday.
Let me go early on Friday.
I'm going to leave early on Friday, OK?

feedback.es: Con un favor grande y una jefa, I was wondering if I might sube el grado de cortesía; las otras dos opciones afirman en vez de pedir.

origin.text: You need your manager to let you leave early on Friday. It is a big favour.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué pide la persona.

choices.text: She offers her notes to a classmate.
She asks a classmate to lend her some notes.
She asks the teacher to repeat the lesson.

feedback.es: La hablante usa «I don't suppose you could» para pedir los apuntes de un compañero y explica por qué: faltó a clase.

origin.audio: I don't suppose you could lend me your notes from yesterday? I missed the class.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Te importaría prestarme tu paraguas?»

feedback.es: Después de Would you mind el verbo va en -ing: lending.

origin.text: Would you mind ___ me your umbrella?

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Sería posible en absoluto salir un poco antes?»

answer.text: Would it be at all possible to leave a bit earlier

feedback.es: Would it be at all possible to + verbo es la fórmula formal; a bit earlier cierra la petición.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase encaja mejor para pedirle un lápiz a tu mejor amigo?

choices.text: Would it be at all possible for you to lend me a pencil?
I don't suppose you could possibly lend me a pencil, could you?
Can you lend me a pencil?

feedback.es: Con un amigo cercano y un favor pequeño, Can you… basta; las fórmulas más largas suenan exageradas para un lápiz.

origin.text: Your best friend is next to you in class and you need a pencil.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué le piden al oyente.

choices.text: To shut the window because of the cold.
To open the window because it is hot.
To turn off the lights in the room.

feedback.es: Would you mind closing… pide cerrar la ventana y el motivo es el frío.

origin.audio: Would you mind closing the window? It's a bit cold in here.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me preguntaba si podrías hacerme un favor.»

feedback.es: Do me a favour es la expresión fija para pedir ayuda; favour se escribe con u en inglés británico.

origin.text: I was wondering if you might do me a ___.

es: Sustituir expresiones crudas por eufemismos y atenuaciones (between jobs, passed away, let go, not the best) al hablar de temas delicados.

teaching.en: Saying “unemployed” is blunt, so many people say “between jobs”.
teaching.es: Decir «desempleado» es brusco, así que mucha gente dice «entre trabajos».
teaching.explanationEs: Between jobs es un eufemismo: suaviza una situación difícil y deja abierta una salida.
teaching.audioText: Saying “unemployed” is blunt, so many people say “between jobs”.

teaching.en: Sadly, my elderly neighbour passed away last week.
teaching.es: Por desgracia, mi vecino mayor falleció la semana pasada.
teaching.explanationEs: Passed away es más suave que died; elderly es más amable que old.
teaching.audioText: Sadly, my elderly neighbour passed away last week.

teaching.en: The company had to let three workers go, so the manager spoke gently.
teaching.es: La empresa tuvo que despedir a tres trabajadores, así que el jefe habló con delicadeza.
teaching.explanationEs: Let someone go es la forma suave de fire (He was let go = lo despidieron); gently describe el tono con que se da la noticia.
segments: The company had to let three workers
go, so the manager spoke gently.
teaching.audioText: The company had to let three workers go, so the manager spoke gently.

teaching.en: Saying “not the best” about a terrible film is a classic understatement.
teaching.es: Decir «no es lo mejor» de una película terrible es una atenuación clásica.
teaching.explanationEs: Not the best rebaja la opinión: el oyente entiende «malo».
segments: terrible film is a classic understatement.
teaching.audioText: Saying “not the best” about a terrible film is a classic understatement.

teaching.en: “Cosy” is often a euphemism for “very small”.
teaching.es: «Acogedor» suele ser un eufemismo de «muy pequeño».
teaching.explanationEs: Los anuncios de pisos usan eufemismos: cosy, compact… El mensaje real es otro.
teaching.audioText: “Cosy” is often a euphemism for “very small”.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase suaviza «The firm fired her»?

choices.text: The firm gave her a new job.
The firm paid her more.
The firm let her go.

feedback.es: «Let go» dice lo mismo que fired sin la palabra dura; las otras dos frases cambian el significado por completo.

hint.es: Busca la frase que dice lo mismo que fired, pero con delicadeza.

prompt.es: Completa: «Mi tío está entre trabajos ahora mismo.»

feedback.es: La expresión fija es between jobs, con jobs en plural.

hint.es: Es el plural de la palabra que significa «empleo».

origin.text: My uncle is between ___ right now.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mi abuela falleció el año pasado.»

answer.text: My grandmother passed away last year
accepted: My grandmother passed away last year
Last year my grandmother passed away

feedback.es: Passed away se escribe con el verbo en pasado y away al final; last year cierra la frase.

hint.es: El verbo con away va justo después del sujeto.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada eufemismo con lo que quiere decir en realidad.

feedback.es: Cada expresión suaviza una idea cruda: muerte, falta de empleo, edad o mala calidad.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué noticia se comenta.

choices.text: A man has died.
A man has lost his job.
A man has moved house.

feedback.es: «Passed away» es la forma suave de «died»: la hablante da el pésame por la muerte del abuelo.

origin.audio: I'm sorry to hear that. Your grandfather was such a kind man. I heard he passed away on Sunday.

prompt.es: Completa: «Decir «desempleado» es demasiado brusco.»

feedback.es: Blunt describe lo que se dice sin suavizar; por eso se prefiere un eufemismo.

origin.text: Saying “unemployed” is too ___.

prompt.es: Elige la frase más suave para decir que despidieron a un compañero.

choices.text: He was fired last week.
He was let go last week.
He was kicked out last week.

feedback.es: «Was let go» suaviza el despido; fired es directo y kicked out es coloquial y duro.

origin.text: You want to tell a friend that a colleague lost his job. You do not want to sound blunt.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige la situación del hermano.

choices.text: He has a new job in another city.
He is on holiday for two weeks.
He has no job now but is searching.

feedback.es: «Between jobs» significa sin empleo por ahora, y el hablante añade que sigue buscando.

origin.audio: My brother is between jobs, but he is looking for something new.

prompt.es: Completa: «El piso es acogedor, o sea, muy pequeño.»

feedback.es: Cosy es el eufemismo típico de los anuncios para un espacio muy pequeño.

origin.text: The flat is “___”, which really means very small.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Por desgracia, el resultado no fue el mejor.»

answer.text: Sadly the result was not the best
accepted: Sadly the result was not the best
The result was sadly not the best

feedback.es: Sadly abre la frase con tono suave y not the best atenúa la mala noticia.

prompt.es: ¿Cómo dirías «old» con más amabilidad en la frase de Ana?

choices.text: My grandfather is elderly, so he lives with us.
My grandfather is unemployed, so he lives with us.
My grandfather is blunt, so he lives with us.

feedback.es: Elderly describe a una persona mayor con respeto; unemployed y blunt hablan de otra cosa: trabajo y carácter.

origin.text: Ana says: “My grandfather is very old, so he lives with us.”

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué opina realmente el hablante.

choices.text: He loved the meal.
He did not enjoy the meal.
He cooked the meal himself.

feedback.es: «Not the best» es una atenuación: quien lo dice quiere decir que no le gustó.

origin.audio: It was not the best meal I have had, to be honest.

prompt.es: Completa: «Leo preguntó si el señor mayor había fallecido.»

feedback.es: En una pregunta transmitida de sí o no se usa if o whether, con orden afirmativo y el verbo un paso atrás: had passed away.

origin.text: Leo asked ___ the elderly man had passed away.

es: Identificar atenuadores (it seems, a bit, slightly, might, I wonder if, I'd suggest) en una consulta médica y entender qué mensaje real esconden.

teaching.en: It seems that your blood pressure is slightly high.
teaching.es: Parece que tu presión arterial está un poco alta.
teaching.explanationEs: It seems that y slightly suavizan la noticia: el mensaje real es «tienes la tensión alta».
teaching.audioText: It seems that your blood pressure is slightly high.

teaching.en: The results are a bit worrying, to be honest.
teaching.es: Los resultados son algo preocupantes, para ser sincero.
teaching.explanationEs: A bit + adjetivo rebaja la noticia; a bit worrying puede significar «preocupante».
teaching.audioText: The results are a bit worrying, to be honest.

teaching.en: I wonder if we could try a different medicine.
teaching.es: Me pregunto si podríamos probar otra medicina.
teaching.explanationEs: I wonder if + could: parece una duda, pero el médico suele proponer un cambio.
teaching.audioText: I wonder if we could try a different medicine.

teaching.en: I'd suggest you rest for a week.
teaching.es: Te sugeriría que descansaras una semana.
teaching.explanationEs: I'd suggest suena amable, pero el médico espera que lo hagas.
teaching.audioText: I'd suggest you rest for a week.

teaching.en: The patient might need a second test next week.
teaching.es: Puede que el paciente necesite otra prueba la semana que viene.
teaching.explanationEs: Might suaviza: en una consulta suele significar que hay que hacerla.
teaching.audioText: The patient might need a second test next week.

prompt.es: ¿Qué mensaje real esconde la frase de la doctora?

choices.text: There is a real problem, said gently.
There is nothing to worry about.
The doctor has lost the results.

feedback.es: Quitando «it seems» y «small», queda una noticia clara: hay un problema real, dicho con suavidad.

hint.es: Quita it seems y small: ¿qué noticia queda?

origin.text: Doctor: “It seems there is a small problem with your results.”

prompt.es: Completa: «Me pregunto si podríamos hacer otra prueba.»

feedback.es: I wonder if we could… presenta una propuesta del médico como si fuera una duda.

origin.text: I ___ if we could do another test.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Parece que tu garganta está un poco roja.»

answer.text: It seems that your throat is slightly red

feedback.es: It seems that abre la frase con distancia y slightly suaviza el adjetivo red.

hint.es: Empieza con el atenuador it seems that y termina con el adjetivo.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada atenuador con el mensaje real del médico.

pairs: I wonder if you could wait.

feedback.es: Cada atenuador rebaja un mensaje concreto: problema, preocupación, instrucción o petición.

pairs: I wonder if you could wait.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué debe hacer la paciente.

choices.text: Run for two more weeks.
Take a break from sport for two weeks.
Go to the hospital tonight.

feedback.es: «I'd suggest you stop running» es una recomendación firme: debe dejar el deporte dos semanas.

origin.audio: I'd suggest you stop running for two weeks. It seems your knee is slightly sore.

prompt.es: Completa: «La paciente debe descansar dos días.»

feedback.es: Patient es el sustantivo para la persona que recibe la consulta médica.

origin.text: The ___ must rest for two days.

prompt.es: ¿Qué espera realmente la doctora de la paciente?

choices.text: That she works more this month.
That she asks the doctor to rest.
That she rests more.

feedback.es: «I wonder if you could…» es una petición suave: la doctora quiere que descanse más este mes.

origin.text: Doctor: “I wonder if you could rest a bit more this month.”

prompt.es: Escucha y elige el mensaje real del médico.

choices.text: Something may be wrong, so a new test is needed.
Everything is perfect and no more tests are needed.
The test on Monday has been cancelled.

feedback.es: «Slightly unusual» y la prueba del lunes indican que puede haber un problema y hay que comprobarlo.

origin.audio: The results are slightly unusual, but we need another test on Monday to be sure.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sugeriría que descansaras unos días.»

feedback.es: I'd suggest you + verbo base: recomendación amable que funciona como instrucción.

origin.text: I'd ___ you rest for a few days.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Parece que los resultados son algo preocupantes.»

answer.text: It seems that the results are a bit worrying

feedback.es: It seems that atenúa la noticia y a bit worrying rebaja el adjetivo.

prompt.es: ¿Qué tipo de mensaje es la frase del médico?

choices.text: A warning that sugar is finished.
A polite instruction to eat less sugar.
A question about the patient's shopping.

feedback.es: «It might be a good idea to» suena a sugerencia, pero el médico espera que el paciente coma menos azúcar.

origin.text: Doctor: “It might be a good idea to cut down on sugar.”

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué noticia da el médico.

choices.text: The result is very good.
The test must be repeated tomorrow.
The result is bad, and the medicine must start.

feedback.es: «Not the best» rebaja la noticia: el resultado no es bueno y hay que empezar la medicina pronto.

origin.audio: To be honest, the result is not the best. I'm afraid we need to start the medicine soon.

prompt.es: Completa: «Su presión parece estar un poco baja.»

feedback.es: Seems to be + adjetivo es el atenuador de distancia más habitual.

origin.text: Her blood pressure ___ to be slightly low.

title.es: Dar una mala noticia con tacto

es: Rechazar con tacto la propuesta de un amigo: reconocer la idea, decir que no con claridad, usar tres atenuadores y ofrecer una alternativa concreta.

teaching.en: Honestly, I'm a bit worried about the budget for this trip.
teaching.es: Sinceramente, me preocupa un poco el presupuesto de este viaje.
teaching.explanationEs: Honestly y a bit son dos atenuadores: das el motivo sin atacar la idea del otro.
segments: Honestly, I'm a bit worried about
teaching.audioText: Honestly, I'm a bit worried about the budget for this trip.

teaching.en: I'm afraid I can't say yes to your proposal.
teaching.es: Me temo que no puedo decir que sí a tu propuesta.
teaching.explanationEs: I'm afraid + can't: el rechazo es claro, pero cortés.
teaching.audioText: I'm afraid I can't say yes to your proposal.

teaching.en: Perhaps it would be better to wait until the money is less tight.
teaching.es: Quizá sería mejor esperar hasta que el dinero esté menos justo.
teaching.explanationEs: Perhaps + would be better: una sugerencia suave que a la vez frena el plan.
segments: Perhaps it would be better to wait
until the money is less tight.
teaching.audioText: Perhaps it would be better to wait until the money is less tight.

teaching.en: How about a cheaper alternative, like a day trip instead?
teaching.es: ¿Qué tal una alternativa más barata, como una excursión de un día en su lugar?
teaching.explanationEs: Un rechazo sin alternativa deja al otro con las manos vacías; How about… instead? la ofrece.
teaching.audioText: How about a cheaper alternative, like a day trip instead?

teaching.en: It's a great idea, but I'd rather do something smaller this time.
teaching.es: Es una gran idea, pero prefiero hacer algo más pequeño esta vez.
teaching.explanationEs: I'd rather + verbo base expresa preferencia suave; but marca el rechazo.
segments: It's a great idea, but I'd
rather do something smaller this time.
teaching.audioText: It's a great idea, but I'd rather do something smaller this time.

prompt.es: Elige el rechazo claro pero cortés a una invitación a una fiesta.

choices.text: I don't know if I come to the party.
I'm afraid I can't come to the party.
I can't come. Bye.

feedback.es: I'm afraid I can't dice no con claridad y cortesía; las otras opciones son confusas o bruscas.

hint.es: Busca la frase que dice no con claridad y empieza con I'm afraid.

prompt.es: Completa: «Quizá sería mejor esperar un poco.»

feedback.es: Perhaps abre una sugerencia suave y suena más elegante que un no directo.

origin.text: ___ it would be better to wait a bit.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Prefiero hacer algo más pequeño esta vez.»

answer.text: I'd rather do something smaller this time
accepted: I'd rather do something smaller this time
This time I'd rather do something smaller

feedback.es: I'd rather + verbo base expresa una preferencia suave; this time cierra la frase.

hint.es: Empieza con I'd rather y sigue con un verbo base.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con la pieza del no amable que cumple.

feedback.es: Cada frase cumple un paso: reconocer, rechazar, dar el motivo o proponer otra cosa.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué alternativa ofrece el hablante.

choices.text: A longer race next month.
A visit to the doctor.
A gentle walk instead of the race.

feedback.es: Tras el motivo (la rodilla), propone «a walk in the park instead»: un paseo en lugar de la carrera.

origin.audio: Thanks for the invitation, Sara, but I'm afraid I can't join the marathon. Honestly, my knee is a bit sore. How about a walk in the park instead?

prompt.es: Completa: «Me preocupa un poco el dinero.»

feedback.es: I'm a bit worried about + nombre da el motivo con un atenuador.

origin.text: I'm a bit ___ about the money.

prompt.es: Elige el rechazo que reconoce, rechaza con tacto y propone algo.

choices.text: It's a great plan, Leo, but I'm afraid I can't this year. How about a small project first?
It's a great plan, Leo, but no.
I can't this year. Find someone else.

feedback.es: Solo la respuesta con I'm afraid I can't this year y una alternativa reconoce la idea, dice no con tacto y propone algo; las otras dejan piezas fuera.

origin.text: Your friend Leo wants to start a business together. You like Leo, but you do not have the money now.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué propone el hablante.

choices.text: To cancel the meeting for ever.
To meet on Saturday.
To go out tonight.

feedback.es: Tras dar su motivo (cansancio), propone quedar el sábado en lugar de esta semana.

origin.audio: I'm a bit tired this week, so I'd rather stay at home. Shall we meet on Saturday instead?

prompt.es: Completa: «Me preocupa el presupuesto de este mes.»

feedback.es: El motivo del rechazo suele ser concreto: the budget explica por qué no puedes.

origin.text: I'm worried about the ___ this month.

prompt.es: Escribe el mensaje: reconoce la idea, rechaza, da el motivo y ofrece una alternativa.

answer.text: Hi Mia, thank you for the invitation. It's a great idea, and I can see why you like it. Honestly, I'm a bit worried about this month. I have exams, and my time is very tight. I'm afraid I can't say yes to a film club every Friday, because I wouldn't be a good host. Perhaps it would be better to wait until the exams are over. How about a film evening once a month instead? We could watch a film at your place next Saturday and then decide together. I'd rather do something small for now. I hope you understand! See you soon, Ana
accepted: Hi Mia, thank you for the invitation. It's a great idea, and I can see why you like it. Honestly, I'm a bit worried about this month. I have exams, and my time is very tight. I'm afraid I can't say yes to a film club every Friday, because I wouldn't be a good host. Perhaps it would be better to wait until the exams are over. How about a film evening once a month instead? We could watch a film at your place next Saturday and then decide together. I'd rather do something small for now. I hope you understand! See you soon, Ana

Hello Mia, thanks for thinking of me. A film club is a nice idea. To be honest, I'm a little tired this month, and the exams are very close. I'm afraid I can't join every Friday, because I need that time to study. Maybe we could start in June, when my exams are finished. What if we watch one film together this Saturday instead? I would bring the snacks and you could choose the film. It would be fun, and we could decide about the club later. I'd rather be honest than say yes and cancel. Speak soon, Ana

feedback.es: Un no amable reconoce la idea, rechaza con claridad, da un motivo con tres atenuadores y propone algo concreto.

origin.text: Tu amiga Mia propone organizar un club de cine todos los viernes en tu casa. Tienes exámenes y poco tiempo este mes. She cancels the plan completely.

es: Transmitir a un tercero dos preguntas de otras personas con preguntas indirectas (asked whether, wanted to know why) y responder con diplomacia usando atenuadores y una solución.

teaching.en: The tenant asked whether the landlord could repair the heating.
teaching.es: El inquilino preguntó si el casero podía reparar la calefacción.
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta indirecta: whether/if, sujeto antes del verbo, sin did ni «?»; could retrocede desde can.
teaching.audioText: The tenant asked whether the landlord could repair the heating.

teaching.en: Mia wanted to know why the rent had gone up.
teaching.es: Mia quería saber por qué había subido el alquiler.
teaching.explanationEs: wanted to know + why + sujeto + verbo: sin inversión; had gone up retrocede un tiempo.
teaching.audioText: Mia wanted to know why the rent had gone up.

teaching.en: Tom wondered whether he could pay the rent a week late.
teaching.es: Tom se preguntaba si podría pagar el alquiler con una semana de retraso.
teaching.explanationEs: Wondered whether transmite una pregunta con tono suave y distante.
segments: Tom wondered whether he could pay
teaching.audioText: Tom wondered whether he could pay the rent a week late.

teaching.en: I'd like to reply to both questions, if I may.
teaching.es: Me gustaría responder a las dos preguntas, si me lo permite.
teaching.explanationEs: If I may suaviza el turno de palabra: tono diplomático.
teaching.audioText: I'd like to reply to both questions, if I may.

teaching.en: That was a diplomatic reply: she said no gently and offered help.
teaching.es: Fue una respuesta diplomática: dijo que no con suavidad y ofreció ayuda.
teaching.explanationEs: Diplomatic = con tacto: rechazo cortés más una solución.
segments: That was a diplomatic reply: she
said no gently and offered help.
teaching.audioText: That was a diplomatic reply: she said no gently and offered help.

prompt.es: Elige cómo se transmite: Tom preguntó «Can the landlord repair the door?»

choices.text: Tom asked whether could the landlord repair the door.
Tom asked whether can the landlord repair the door.
Tom asked whether the landlord could repair the door.

feedback.es: En la pregunta transmitida el sujeto va antes del verbo y can pasa a could.

hint.es: Pon el sujeto antes del verbo y cambia can por could.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sara quería saber por qué estaba apagada la calefacción.»

feedback.es: Wanted to know + why introduce la pregunta indirecta: sin did ni inversión.

hint.es: Es el verbo que significa «saber» y sigue a wanted to.

origin.text: Sara wanted to ___ why the heating was off.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Tom se preguntaba si el casero respondería pronto.»

answer.text: Tom wondered whether the landlord would reply soon

feedback.es: Wondered whether + sujeto + would + verbo base: pregunta indirecta con tono suave.

hint.es: Empieza con Tom wondered whether y termina con soon.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fórmula para transmitir una pregunta con su significado.

feedback.es: Asked whether y wondered if introducen una pregunta de sí o no; wanted to know why introduce la de motivo; replied that presenta la respuesta, no una pregunta.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige las dos preguntas que se transmiten.

choices.text: If the heating can be fixed, and if the rent will rise.
If the landlord is in, and why the heating is off.
If the rent can be paid late, and how long the repair takes.

feedback.es: Se transmiten dos preguntas: si se puede arreglar la calefacción y si el alquiler volverá a subir.

origin.audio: Tom asked whether the heating could be repaired on Monday. Mia wanted to know if the rent would go up again.

prompt.es: Completa: «Leo quería saber cuándo llegaría el casero.»

feedback.es: Las preguntas con palabra interrogativa la conservan: when + sujeto + would + verbo.

origin.text: Leo wanted to know ___ the landlord would arrive.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál es la versión correcta al transmitir la pregunta de Mia?

choices.text: Mia wanted to know why hadn't the landlord answered her message.
Mia wanted to know why the landlord hadn't answered her message.
Mia wanted to know why the landlord hasn't answered my message.

feedback.es: Solo hadn't answered her mantiene el orden afirmativo, retrocede el tiempo y cambia el pronombre; las otras dos invierten el orden o dejan el tiempo sin cambiar.

origin.text: Mia's direct question: “Why hasn't the landlord answered my message?”

prompt.es: Escucha la respuesta de la casera y elige qué decide.

choices.text: She refuses the repair and lowers the rent.
She agrees to both requests immediately.
She agrees to repair it but refuses to change the rent.

feedback.es: Acepta la reparación («will start on Thursday») pero rechaza cambiar el alquiler («I'm afraid the rent cannot change»).

origin.audio: I understand your concern, and I wonder if we could find a solution together. The repair will start on Thursday, but I'm afraid the rent cannot change this year.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me gustaría responder, si me lo permite.»

feedback.es: If I may es una fórmula cortés para pedir la palabra.

origin.text: I'd like to reply, if I ___.

prompt.es: Escribe el mensaje a la casera: transmite las dos preguntas y responde con tacto.

answer.text: Dear Sara, thank you for your message. I understand that some tenants have paid late, and I wonder if we could find a simple solution together. Honestly, I think the start of the month is a bit difficult for some people. Before that, I would like to pass on two questions. Tom asked whether you could repair the heating before Friday, because it seems to be getting colder. Mia wanted to know why the rent had gone up this year. I'm afraid I can't answer that, so I would be grateful for your reply. Perhaps we could agree on a payment date on the same day each month instead. I'd like to thank you in advance, and I hope this is fine for you. Best wishes, Leo
accepted: Dear Sara, thank you for your message. I understand that some tenants have paid late, and I wonder if we could find a simple solution together. Honestly, I think the start of the month is a bit difficult for some people. Before that, I would like to pass on two questions. Tom asked whether you could repair the heating before Friday, because it seems to be getting colder. Mia wanted to know why the rent had gone up this year. I'm afraid I can't answer that, so I would be grateful for your reply. Perhaps we could agree on a payment date on the same day each month instead. I'd like to thank you in advance, and I hope this is fine for you. Best wishes, Leo

Hello Sara, thank you for writing. I'm sorry that some rent has arrived late, and I wonder if a fixed date could help everyone. It might be a bit hard for people to pay on the first day. I have two questions from my flatmates. Tom wondered whether the heating could be repaired before Friday, since it seems to be getting colder every night. Mia asked why the rent had gone up this year, and she would like to hear your reply. I'd suggest that we talk about both points on Saturday, if that is convenient. What if we agree on a fixed date each month instead? Thank you for your patience, and I hope we can find a fair answer. Kind regards, Leo

feedback.es: Un buen mensaje transmite las dos preguntas con whether/why sin inversión, responde a la queja con atenuadores y propone una solución concreta.

origin.text: Eres el representante de un piso compartido. La casera, Sara, te escribió: «Algunos inquilinos pagan tarde.» Tom preguntó si ella podía arreglar la calefacción antes del viernes, y Mia quiso saber por qué subió el alquiler este año. Escribe entre 110 y 150 palabras: transmite las dos preguntas con estructuras indirectas, responde a la queja con al menos dos atenuadores y propón una solución.

prompt.es: ¿Cómo transmites la pregunta de Carlos a otra persona?

choices.text: Carlos wanted to know when the landlord would fix the window.
Carlos wanted to know when will the landlord fix the window.
Carlos wanted to know when you will fix the window.

feedback.es: La pregunta transmitida mantiene el orden afirmativo, retrocede will a would y sustituye you por the landlord.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige el mensaje real detrás de los atenuadores.

choices.text: The rent will go down next year.
The rent will rise, and she wants to discuss it.
The weekend meeting is cancelled.

feedback.es: «It seems» y «a bit» suavizan la noticia: el alquiler va a subir, y «perhaps we could talk» propone hablar de ello.

origin.audio: I'm sorry to say this, but it seems the rent will go up a bit next year. Perhaps we could talk about it at the weekend.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Mia se preguntaba por qué el casero no había respondido.»

answer.text: Mia wondered why the landlord had not replied

feedback.es: Wondered why + sujeto + had + participio: pregunta indirecta con el verbo un paso atrás.
